name: Rotary UPS
summary: A UPS built around a rotating synchronous machine with kinetic storage, often coupled to a diesel engine for long backup.
description: A rotary UPS uses a synchronous machine running continuously on the critical bus, with stored kinetic energy in a flywheel or induction coupling bridging the gap until a coupled diesel engine starts and takes over. A choke between the utility and the critical bus lets the machine condition the supply and isolate the load from network faults.

Single-line diagrams show the incoming utility feeder, a series choke, the synchronous machine with its kinetic energy module and clutch to the engine, and the critical and sometimes non-critical outputs. A bypass path around the unit is normally drawn.

The machine provides real short-circuit current, unlike a static UPS, which helps downstream protection discriminate. The symbol does not show the ride-through time to engine pickup or the choke impedance, both of which matter for design.
readingNotes: Identify the choke between the utility and critical bus.
Check engine coupling and the kinetic module.
drawingChecklist: State machine rating and ride-through time.
Show choke, engine coupling and bypass.
distinction: A rotary UPS uses rotating machines and kinetic storage; a static UPS uses power electronics and a battery.
